Hans Gugelot, Kodak Carousel S slide projector, 1963

Hans Gugelot’s redesign of the Kodak round-tray projector for Europe: a square grey box under a clear-lidded slide ring, with small black controls.

Source
Museum Ulm/HfG-Archiv, HfG-Ar MS 0156 (museum-digital)
Creator
Hans Gugelot (form design); Kodak AG, Stuttgart
Made
1963
Style
Ulm School (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Precise, practical, calm
Evidence
Inspected the HfG-Archiv image of object HfG-Ar MS 0156 at 960 × 669 px through museum-digital. The case of this copy reads “Kodak Carousel S-AV”, a variant of the S. A second photograph, of a “Carousel S” on the Die Neue Sammlung website (1800 × 1371 px), shows the same form. Its object number could not be read, because the page loads its text by script.
Reviewed
2 October 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The HfG-Archiv record credits Kodak AG (Stuttgart) with the manufacture and Hans Gugelot (1920–1965) with the form design, both 1963, and gives metal and electronics, 26 × 26 cm, 15 cm high. museum-digital 2088570.

The record says that in the early 1960s Kodak Germany commissioned Gugelot’s “institut für produktgestaltung und design e.V.” in Neu-Ulm to redesign the round-tray projector for Europe. Gugelot bevelled the tray edge so that slides were easier to take out, and added a Plexiglas lid against dust. museum-digital.

Observed

  • The body is a square, matte grey box with slightly rounded vertical edges and a thin seam around its middle.
  • A round black slide tray sits on top, edged with a ring of small white numerals, under a clear flat lid.
  • The lens, a slide slot, and a knurled knob are black. A small vent of vertical slots sits on one side.
  • The name “Kodak Carousel S-AV” is printed small in white on the grey side, with “Kodak” in bold.
  • There is no colored accent.

Why it belongs

The projector shows the Ulm method outside Braun: a technical object made calm by one grey volume, one radius, and small black controls.

Borrow

Put a numbered scale around a circular control, in small white figures on black.
